method: Independent source-based reading by /root/teaching_readings, separate from both teaching authors and the question-bank author. All 25 rendered pages, extracted native text and speaker notes, all 34 original embedded images, and all 24 nonuniform temporal phase grids covering 24 samples from each of eight videos were inspected before authoring the guide and core selection. Readable individual video frames and full-resolution complex source figures supplemented the grids. Every final teaching entry and all 50 question stems, keys, answers, rubrics, sources, and all 100 MCQ options with feedback were read and compared with that evidence. The guide/core additions were authored by this reviewer after source review, so their authoring is not represented as a separate independent review.
sourceAndTeachingChecks: The 100–500 Hz membrane frequencies are assigned illustrative harmonics, not claimed natural eigenfrequencies. Equal pickup peaks are engineered locally, and the combined panel uses reduced vertical magnification.

Fixed displacement node and free displacement antinode yield odd quarter-wave counts and odd harmonics. The 100 Hz examples are separately tuned; at fixed length and wave speed the fixed–free fundamental is half the fixed–fixed fundamental.
Air motion is longitudinal and oscillatory. Particle excursion is distinguished from changing neighbor spacing, and the moving Schwa reference is not described as a stationary baseline.

Constriction effects depend on mode-specific local motion versus compression: /u/ lowers F1 and F2, /i/ near two-thirds lowers F1 and raises F2, and /a/ near one-third raises F1 and lowers F2 in the qualitative source model. No measured numerical shifts are invented.

Source F0 values 100, 250 and 350 Hz change harmonic spacing within the same frequency window. Filter targets and colored harmonic samples remain distinct, including close /a/ targets 800/900 Hz in this lecture-specific schematic.

Spectrum frequency maps to spectrogram height, spectrum amplitude to darkness, and time advances horizontally. The original base and both overlays were inspected separately to recover the two reveal steps.
The network uses ordered F1/F2 inputs, hidden widths 3/2/4 and five word outputs in the printed order. All forty signed connection weights are retained in teaching and match the native groups.

Displayed p(word) values [.5,.1,.1,.1,.2] are identified as schematic probabilities rather than a demonstrated result of the forty random linear weights. No target label or measured recognition accuracy is inferred.

The PyTorch declaration has four bias-free Linear layers and no activation, probability normalization, explicit input call, assignment of the pictured weights or training procedure. Architecture, inference and learning remain distinct.

guideAndCorePreservation.selectionRationale: Seven of twenty-five source pages cover boundary conditions, the general local perturbation mechanism, source–filter integration, acoustic representation, architecture, inference evidence and executable declaration. The new readiness guide links all three vowel perturbations without automatically marking every recap or demonstration as core.

descriptiveMetrics.interpretation: Mechanical counts describe the frozen bank; source validity and distinct reasoning demands were judged by reading.

retainedSourceLimitations: Video review covers 24 nonuniform temporal samples per video and readable individual phases, not an assertion of continuous frame-by-frame playback. The probe confirms no audio stream in any of the eight videos.
Several original air-column video titles are cropped at the right edge. Readable labels, the motion and native reasoning establish the supported content; the missing edge is not invented.
The Popquiz page supplies A–F without a question stem or answer key, and F wraps in the static rendering. No letter-specific answer or exact particle alignment is invented.
The reflection and favorite-experiment headings supply no experiment setup or result. They are not expanded into invented teaching or assessment evidence.
The p23 key names negative weights orange although their rendered labels are green. Signed numeric labels are the reliable evidence.

The p24 speaker notes describe looping dots and a smiley, but slide24.xml contains only cSld/clrMapOvr, with no timing sequence, and the static glyph is an angry face. Intended flow order is explained without claiming verified temporal playback, a correct target or a demonstrated classification error.
The original /i/ or /I/ row label is retained literally. Its alternate character is not silently changed to an inferred phonetic symbol.
